topics.title: Science Around Us
objectives: Student can identify scientific phenomena in daily life activities like cooking, rusting, and weather changes
Student can list three daily observations that can be investigated scientifically
visualIdeas: a collage of daily activities such as boiling milk, a plant growing, and a rusting nail with magnifying glasses over them
a table comparing common sense assumptions with scientifically verified facts

topics.title: Asking Questions and Exploring
objectives: Student can formulate questions about natural events starting with why, how, and what
Student can classify questions into testable and non-testable categories
visualIdeas: a flowchart showing a question branching into testable by experiment and not testable by experiment
illustrations of a curious child observing a falling leaf and writing down questions on a notepad

topics.title: Scientific Methods of Enquiry
objectives: Student can arrange the steps of a scientific investigation in the correct chronological order
Student can draw a simple diagram representing the cycle of hypothesis, experiment, observation, and conclusion
visualIdeas: a circular cycle chart of the scientific method steps with distinct colored blocks
a comic strip of a student solving the mystery of a flashlight not working by checking its batteries

topics.title: Plants Around Us
objectives: Student can classify plants into herbs, shrubs, trees, climbers, and creepers based on their stem structure and height
Student can draw and label the root system, stem, leaves, and flowers of a typical plant
visualIdeas: a comparison grid showing drawings of a coriander plant, rose bush, mango tree, money plant, and pumpkin plant
a detailed labelled diagram of a plant showing root, shoot, leaf, and flower

topics.title: Animals Around Us
objectives: Student can categorize animals based on their habitats like terrestrial, aquatic, aerial, and arboreal
Student can identify outer physical body structures of animals that assist in movement
visualIdeas: a landscape drawing depicting aerial, arboreal, terrestrial, and aquatic zones
close-up drawings of a fish fin, a bird wing, and a dog leg highlighting movement structures

topics.title: Grouping Plants and Animals
objectives: Student can group a given list of organisms based on shared physical characteristics
Student can state the similarities and differences between plants and animals
visualIdeas: a Venn diagram comparing plants and animals based on movement, food synthesis, and cellular structure
a sorting game layout with drag-and-drop boxes for grouping birds, insects, and mammals

topics.title: Why Classify
objectives: Student can explain the necessity of classification in studying a large variety of organisms efficiently
Student can identify how classification systems help in naming and organizing new discoveries
visualIdeas: a split illustration showing a messy pile of books versus a neatly organized library shelf
a tree diagram showing the hierarchical division of living things into broad kingdoms down to individual species

chapters.title: Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body

topics.title: What is in Our Food
objectives: Student can list the major food items consumed across different regions of India
Student can identify the raw ingredients used to prepare common food dishes
visualIdeas: an outline map of India with popular regional dishes represented pictorially
a recipe breakout diagram showing a plate of rice pudding connected by lines to its raw ingredients

topics.title: Nutrients in Food
objectives: Student can name the five main classes of nutrients required by the human body
Student can match each nutrient to its primary role as energy-giving, body-building, or protective
visualIdeas: a segmented plate displaying carbohydrates, fats, proteins, vitamins, and minerals with corresponding food sources
a table classifying nutrients into energy providers, growth promoters, and disease fighters

topics.title: Testing for Nutrients
objectives: Student can describe the steps of testing for the presence of starch, proteins, and fats in a food sample
Student can identify the positive color change reactions for iodine, copper sulfate, and caustic soda tests
visualIdeas: a step-by-step chemical test strip drawing showing iodine solution turning blue-black on a potato slice
a visual sequence of adding copper sulfate and caustic soda to milk, turning it violet

topics.title: Balanced Diet and Deficiencies
objectives: Student can design a balanced diet chart using locally available, inexpensive food materials
Student can match common deficiency diseases like scurvy, rickets, and anemia with the lack of specific vitamins or minerals
visualIdeas: a balanced food plate showing correct proportions of grains, vegetables, proteins, and dairy
a simple reference table listing vitamin/mineral deficiencies and symptoms with illustrative cartoon icons

topics.title: Magnetic and Non-magnetic Materials
objectives: Student can distinguish between magnetic and non-magnetic substances using a bar magnet
Student can list common daily materials made of iron, nickel, or cobalt that are attracted to magnets

a bar magnet with curved magnetic field lines attracting iron paper clips while ignoring wooden pencils

topics.title: Poles of a Magnet
objectives: Student can locate the north and south poles of a magnet by observing the accumulation of iron filings
Student can state that magnetic poles always exist in pairs and cannot be isolated
visualIdeas: a bar magnet dipped in iron filings, showing thick clusters of filings at the two ends
a sequence drawing showing a bar magnet being cut in half, with new poles appearing on each broken piece

topics.title: Finding Directions with a Magnet
objectives: Student can explain how a freely suspended bar magnet aligns itself in the north-south direction
Student can draw the structural components of a magnetic compass
visualIdeas: a suspended bar magnet tied to a thread from a wooden stand, pointing north-south with a compass underneath
a top-down view of a classic compass dial with the needle pointing to the North mark

topics.title: Magnetic Attraction and Repulsion
objectives: Student can state the rule of magnetic interaction between like and unlike poles
Student can predict the movement of two toy cars fitted with magnets when brought close to each other
visualIdeas: two pairs of bar magnets showing north-south attracting and north-north repelling
a cartoon diagram of magnetic toy cars demonstrating push and pull forces

topics.title: Measuring Distances
objectives: Student can explain why non-standard units of measurement like handspan, cubit, and footstep vary from person to person

a standard measuring tape and ruler placed next to objects of varying lengths

topics.title: Standard Units of Measurement

a timeline of standard measurement benchmarks like the international prototype metre

topics.title: Types of Motion

topics.title: Identifying Materials

a comparative diagram of a hard iron block and a soft sponge being pressed

objectives: Student can group objects as transparent, translucent, or opaque based on light transmission

two beakers, one with salt dissolving completely and another with sand settling at the bottom

topics.title: Concept of Temperature

objectives: Student can state the unit of temperature measurement in Celsius and Fahrenheit scales

a comparison of Celsius and Fahrenheit marking ranges side by side

topics.title: Thermometers
